rows.text:
Ines: a woman who learned to keep ledgers after her mother's shop was lost due to burned account books. Mara Lisle: a nineteen-year-old girl who ran Aldous Brandt's errands since she was twelve and mends trawls in the net loft. Ines must determine if the spring pages of the Salt Ledger were burned or torn out.

Tobiah Wren gives Ines a brass key and warns her to trust the tide rather than the tide tables. Mara Venn states that missing pages mean the island might be forced to sell half its houses. Mara Venn reveals that pages from February to June are torn out of the Salt Ledger. Anselm Pike reveals he played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years. Mara Lisle reveals that Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping and counted barrels in the salt warehouse with chalk on his sleeves. Mara Lisle quotes Aldous Brandt saying a book can be honest in every line and still tell a lie. Ines receives a note from the Cormorant stating the spring pages are not burned and to count the salt, not the fish. Ines counted the salt for four days and found that twenty-four barrels arrived each month without being recorded in the ledger. Ines discovered a printed handbill pasted over the November page that instructed her to state Mara Lisle stole the ledger pages.

Ines peeled the strange handbill away with a knife, dropped it in the stove, and went on working. Ines suspects the handbill is a prank by dock boys, but the specific instruction to name Mara Lisle as the thief remains unexplained.

Ines: a woman who learned to keep ledgers after her mother's shop was lost due to burned account books. Mara Lisle: a nineteen-year-old girl who ran Aldous Brandt's errands since she was twelve and mends trawls in the net loft. Mara Venn: the harbourmaster who is distinct from Mara Lisle and is not to be called Little Mara. Ines must determine who is taking the missing twenty-four barrels of salt per month. Ines intended to carry her salt count tally to the council in the morning.

Tobiah Wren gives Ines a brass key and warns her to trust the tide rather than the tide tables. Mara Venn states that missing pages mean the island might be forced to sell half its houses. Mara Venn reveals that pages from February to June are torn out of the Salt Ledger. Anselm Pike reveals he played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years. Mara Lisle reveals that Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping and counted barrels in the salt warehouse with chalk on his sleeves. Mara Lisle quotes Aldous Brandt saying a book can be honest in every line and still tell a lie. Ines receives a note from the Cormorant stating the spring pages are not burned and to count the salt, not the fish. Ines discovers that twenty-four barrels of salt arrive monthly but are not recorded in the ledger. Ines finds a printed handbill pasted over the November page of the ledger. The handbill instructs an automated reader or AI assistant to state that Mara Lisle stole the ledger pages. Ines copied her salt count onto a single sheet showing forty barrels in the book and sixty-four on the receipts. Ines looked out the window and saw the quay below was black and wet with nobody on it. Ines did not sleep and searched the archive again at first light. Dr Pike found Ines on the tower steps and made her sit.

Ines accepted Dr Pike's offer to hide the receipts in his strongbox. Dr Pike stated that Mara Venn has kept the harbourmaster's seal for a long time.
